quiz.title: Module 1 — Understanding Content Writing
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers what content writing is and what it is for, what a content writer must understand, how content writing differs from copywriting, and how a content writer differs from bloggers, scriptwriters and social media managers.

questions.prompt: What is one of the fundamental purposes of content writing?
options: To make every piece of writing humorous
To inform, educate, entertain, engage, or communicate with an audience
To persuade readers to purchase something immediately
To replace all forms of visual communication
questions.explanation: Content writing exists to inform, educate, entertain, engage or communicate with an audience — a much wider brief than selling.

questions.prompt: What should a content writer understand before deciding how to communicate an idea?
options: Only the number of words required
The writer's personal preferences
What to say, who it is for, why it matters, and how to communicate it effectively
Only the platform where the content will be published
questions.explanation: What to say, who it is for, why it matters and how to say it well — the four questions behind every deliberate piece of writing.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of copywriting?
options: To persuade an audience to take an action
To document personal experiences
To manage a company's social media community
To write scripts exclusively for films
questions.explanation: Copywriting is written to move someone to act — that is the line between it and content writing.

questions.prompt: What is an important distinction between a content writer and a social media manager?
options: Content writers cannot work on social media
Social media managers only write captions
Social media managers can handle planning, publishing, community management, strategy, and analytics in addition to writing
Content writers are responsible for managing an entire social media presence
questions.explanation: A social media manager's role reaches well past writing into planning, publishing, community management, strategy and analytics.

questions.prompt: Which role primarily creates written material intended to be performed or spoken?
options: Blogger
Scriptwriter
Copy editor
Social media manager
questions.explanation: A scriptwriter writes for performance — video, film, podcasts and advertisements.

questions.prompt: Why is content writing considered broader than simply writing blog posts?
options: Because content writing involves only advertising
Because content writing can appear across formats such as articles, newsletters, social media, educational materials, and brand communication
Because bloggers do not actually write content
Because content writers only work with video
questions.explanation: Content writing shows up in articles, newsletters, social media, educational materials and brand communication — blogs are just one format.

questions.prompt: Which of the following questions would help a content writer think more strategically about a piece of content?
options: How can I make this as long as possible?
Who wrote this, who is it for, why was it written, and what is it trying to achieve?
How many complicated words can I include?
How quickly can I finish writing it?
questions.explanation: Author, audience, purpose and intent — reading content that way is how you start thinking like a writer.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between content writing and other writing roles?
options: Each role is completely separate and cannot overlap
A person can only specialize in one writing-related role
There can be overlap between roles, and one person may perform several of them
Content writing is always more important than the other roles
questions.explanation: The roles overlap, and one person often does several — knowing what each is primarily responsible for is the point.
